items.title: nixos/ly: validate generated configuration

items.content_html:
This change adds debug reporting for NixOS facter-generated configuration.

It introduces an internal hardware.facter.changes option used by facter modules to record the values they contribute, and adds a new hardware.facter.debug.changes helper command to inspect those contributions alongside the final retained NixOS values.

The reporting format is now consistent across facter modules: contributions are recorded under the target option path with a module-specific source key, which makes it easier to understand where a generated setting came from and to debug cases where the final merged configuration differs from the value suggested by facter.

This also refactors the facter system module to avoid the previous infinite recursion during evaluation when exposing facter-generated changes, and updates the facter module documentation with the annotation format and the new debug command usage.

Example output:

# facter disk = ["ahci","sd_mod","usb_storage"]
# facter keyboard = ["ehci_pci","xhci_pci"]
# facter virtualisation = []
boot.initrd.availableKernelModules = ["aes","af_alg","ahci","algif_skcipher","ata_piix","atkbd","autofs","blake2b-256","blowfish","cbc","crc32c","cryptd","dm_crypt","dm_mod","ecb","efivarfs","ehci_hcd","ehci_pci","hid_apple","hid_cherry","hid_corsair","hid_generic","hid_lenovo","hid_logitech_dj","hid_logitech_hidpp","hid_microsoft","hid_roccat","i8042","input_leds","lrw","mmc_block","nvme","ohci_hcd","ohci_pci","pata_marvell","pcips2","sata_nv","sata_sis","sata_uli","sata_via","sd_mod","serpent","sha1","sha256","sha512","sr_mod","tpm-crb","tpm-tis","twofish","uhci_hcd","usb_storage","usbhid","xhci_hcd","xhci_pci","xts","xxhash64"]

# facter virtualisation = []
boot.initrd.kernelModules = ["btrfs","dm_mod","i915"]

# facter virtualisation = ["kvm-intel"]
boot.kernelModules = ["atkbd","ctr","kvm-intel","loop"]

# facter bluetooth = true
hardware.bluetooth.enable = true

# facter firmware = true
hardware.cpu.intel.updateMicrocode = true

# facter firmware = true
hardware.enableRedistributableFirmware = true

items.title: nixos/nixos-generate-config: reoder LUKS and LVM

items.content_html:
Previously, if virtual devices (like LVM logical volumes) were contained within a LUKS device, mounting the virtual device would not pull in the hardware config to decrypt the LUKS device (when using the script to generate the hardware config). This would cause the OS to not decrypt the LUKS device and be unable to mount the currently mounted device after the next boot. Now, we will recursively search for any LUKS devices that needs to be decrypted in order to mount the device.

Fixes #490144

items.title: iproute2: modernize

items.content_html:
This PR does several improvements to the junit XML reporting feature of the nixos test driver.

  1. The logic to create reports has been outsourced into a dedicated module test_reporter.py. This separates concerns between logging test output (in Logger.py) and reporting the status of the subtests.

  2. The test report is now a nix output of the test and always provided. It can be accessed via

    nix build .#nixosTests.simple.junitXmlReport
cat result-junitXmlReport/results.xml

    The previous way to create the report by specifying --junit-xml when running the test driver executable is still supported but could be removed in the future since accessing the report from the output of the test derivation is more convenient.

  3. The test report is now created with the junitparser library which is actively maintained. The junit_xml library which we were using before has not seen any maintenance activity since Feb 2020.

This PR enables us to remove the self grown logger in the future as attempted in #509687.

items.content_html:
Partially fixes #27789 by using matching devices found in /dev/disk/by-label/* before using any found in /dev/disk/by-uuid/*.

Wil T's install tutorial explains the motivation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axOxLJ4BWmY&t=1295s

Description of changes

This doesn't change any packages; only newly generated hardware configurations are affected.

This does NOT fix #27789 as originally reported (I was not able to repro that myself), but does address this comment.

At some point the automatic detection of device labels broke and device UUIDs began taking precedent over labels. This makes setting up a new computer a more manual and error-prone process than it needs to be.

With this change, I can instead use the devices generated as-is in hardware-configuration.nix on reinstall.

Previously, when using systemd-networkd (networking.useNetworkd = true)
and disabling systemd-resolved (services.resolved = false), /etc/resolv.conf
was left empty, ignoring networking.nameservers.

This commit ensures that a static /etc/resolv.conf is generated from
networking.nameservers whenever systemd-resolved is disabled, restoring
expected DNS resolution behavior.

Fixes: #445496

items.title: nixos/rnsd: init

items.content_html:
Another attempt at a module for https://github.com/vouch/vouch-proxy. Should address #299381 (comment).

The module is intended to run one instance of vouch-proxy per domain/app to be protected (that is, per entry in services.vouch-proxy.clients), as oauth2 clients should not be shared between applications. By default, it configures every nginx virtualHost matched by a services.vouch-proxy.clients.domain to use vouch-proxy.

Minimal working example below, where everything runs on the same host.
services.nginx.virtualHosts.myAppDomain1 and services.nginx.virtualHosts.myAppDomain2 are already defined as they would be without vouch-proxy, and with the clients myoauthclient1 and myoauthclient2 configured for vouch-proxy in the oauth2 provider.
This example uses kanidm, which the module takes care of (for every client) on vouch-proxy's side if kanidmUrl is set.
For other oauth2 providers, the correct auth_url, token_url and user_info_url need to be set under settings.oauth, either globally or, if required (as is with kanidm for user_info_url), per client.

  services.vouch-proxy = {
    enable = true;
    kanidmUrl = config.services.kanidm.server.settings.domain;
  };

  services.vouch-proxy.clients = {
    myoauthclient1 = {
      port = 12345;
      domain = "myAppDomain1";
      environmentFile = "./myApp1.env"; # this file should contain `VOUCH_JWT_SECRET` and `OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`
    };
    myoauthclient2 = {
      port = 23456;
      domain = "myAppDomain2";
      environmentFile = "./myApp2.env";
    };
  };

    • x86_64-linux
    • aarch64-linux

items.content_html:
#480686 made getty unconditional, fixing several bugs and bad interactions. This imposes no runtime costs due to lazy systemd-based activation, but it does drag getty and its closure in to images. For many NixOS installations, this is fine - they want console login and such anyway - but it's a burden on lights-out containers aiming for minimal image sizes.

This change adds a new configuration knob to totally disable getty for these sorts of headless/lights-out/appliance-style set-ups. The option's description is deliberately made stern to hopefully dissuade anyone from toggling it if their system isn't in that class. As the option defaults to enabling getty, there should be no behaviour change for anyone not explicitly opting themselves in - hopefully with full knowledge of the consequences.

My local testing chopped a whole 15% off one of my images by being able to remove getty (the big contributor being util-linux and its friends), and that's just for one random image - others might be even bigger relative gains. I think that's more than enough to justify this configuration knob.

I had a look for uses of getty in NixOS to see if anywhere wanted to either have a hard dependency on getty and hence explicitly enable it (so that weird configurations get picked up at evaluation time rather than runtime) or disable it. The use sites fall into two categories:

  1. Virtualised set-ups that wire up units to getty listening on ttyS0. These probably don't want a hard dependency: it's reasonable to run these lights-out, and just disabling getty will DTRT here.

  2. modules/profiles/headless.nix, which disables some of the getty units. This could instead disable getty as a whole, but that might break e.g. machinectl shell, and I can imagine set-ups where you want that even without console login, so I have left it alone. Maybe someone else feels differently and more strongly, and then that someone else can put together a PR and argue their case.

Continues #446307

This PR is created in order to have some smaller commits to understand the changes easier... I recommend to read commit-by-commit to understand the changes although I have to admit that some changes could be splitted to even smaller commits.

Compared to the previous PR, this fully uses systemd.tmpfiles for the file management which fixes the case that when the user sets some different paths that the module doesn't break...

A follow-up PR could be done to do the same for the crowdsec-firewall-bouncer.
